cases.applicable_actor: Employers with at least 11 covered individuals, state agencies and political subdivisions; see section 7 for scope.
cases.regulated_action: Use of automated decision outputs in hiring, firing and other employment decisions.
cases.concrete_requirements: No exclusive automated reliance; predeployment validation, annual independent bias testing with public results, experienced human corroboration, disclosure, and human dispute/appeal channels.
cases.differences_and_limits: More extensive safeguards than SC S 443; a different experienced human hears an appeal. The employer definition excludes labor organizations except in their employer role. This is proposed text in the stored introduced version.
cases.selection_reason: Baseline topic 4 rank 3; employment case with operative oversight and appeal provisions.

cases.applicable_actor: Employers using automated applicant or resume screening.
cases.regulated_action: Hiring decisions assisted by automated systems.
cases.concrete_requirements: Meaningful human evaluation before final/adverse decisions, override authority, notice of automated use and data types, and human review on an unsuccessful applicant's request.
cases.differences_and_limits: This short hiring-focused bill does not establish the same annual independent testing package as IN H 1421; the cited sections should not be generalized to every employment decision.
cases.selection_reason: Within baseline topic 4 high-weight candidate pool; second jurisdiction for employment oversight.

passages.start: Section 211-b. Human review of resume screening and hiring decisions.

cases.applicable_actor: Health coverage decision makers, with supervision and review by a health care professional as cross-referenced in the bill.
cases.regulated_action: Automated coverage decisions, including modification or denial of provider authorization requests.
cases.concrete_requirements: No coverage action based solely on AI/tool results; professional supervision and meaningful review when automated tools inform modification or denial of authorization.
cases.differences_and_limits: The title/summary says licensed physician, but operative subsection (C) says health care professional (section 44-30-20). No applicant notice, annual audit or human appeal package is stated in this short stored bill. The referenced definition was not independently examined.
cases.selection_reason: Baseline topic 4 despite Health Use category; directly tests the employment/health human-oversight hypothesis.

passages.start: (B) No actions shall be taken concerning healthcare coverage decisions
passages.end: provision of health care services to insureds.

cases.applicable_actor: Landlords using automated housing screening tools.
cases.regulated_action: Automated screening of applicants for housing.
cases.concrete_requirements: Annual disparate-impact analysis by an independent auditor; public analysis summary; notice about use, characteristics and data; denial reasons; at least 24-hour prior notice enabling an alternative selection process or accommodation request.
cases.differences_and_limits: An alternative process/accommodation request is not an explicit universal right to a human override. Tool scope excludes non-discretionary software. Stored text is S 6471-A, while the source identifier omits the amendment suffix.
cases.selection_reason: Baseline topic 4 high-weight housing case, compared with lending and employment obligations.

passages.end: applicants who were not selected by the tool.

cases.applicable_actor: Covered banking organizations and licensed lenders, excluding listed federal institutions.
cases.concrete_requirements: At least annual impact assessments signed by responsible human reviewers, assessments before material changes, public final reports, notice, and a 30-day correction/appeal route for denials based on incorrect personal information.
cases.differences_and_limits: The appeal is conditional on incorrect personal information. Human review of an impact assessment does not establish review of every loan decision. The housing bill specifies an independent auditor; this text specifies signatures of responsible reviewers. Stored version is S 8115-B; federal banks and other listed institutions are excluded.
cases.selection_reason: Baseline topic 4; source category is only Private Sector Use, but the text identifies lending as a distinct application.

cases.applicable_actor: Illinois Future of Work Task Force.
cases.regulated_action: Study of technology's effects on work and preparation of policy recommendations.
cases.concrete_requirements: Assess emerging technologies and workforce effects, propose training and other policies, and submit a final report to the Governor and General Assembly.
cases.differences_and_limits: Dissolves on filing its final report; broader future-of-work remit than AI alone. IN H 1421 shares the Effect on Labor/Employment label but imposes direct employer obligations rather than establishing a study body. Repeated Illinois companion/version summaries are not independent evidence.
cases.selection_reason: Baseline topic 3 rank 1; retain only one Illinois Future of Work record in the case sample.

passages.start: Section 10. Illinois Future of Work Task Force; duties and responsibilities.
passages.end: apprenticeship programs for the jobs of the future.
is dissolved upon the filing of its report.

cases.applicable_actor: Utah Artificial Intelligence in Education Task Force.
cases.regulated_action: Study and guidance on AI in public and higher education.
cases.concrete_requirements: Study and recommend education AI policies, privacy safeguards and implementation guidelines; coordinate with the AI policy office; meet at least quarterly and report annually to legislative education committees.
cases.differences_and_limits: Annual reporting contrasts with Illinois's final report and dissolution. The text addresses student privacy and educational agency without imposing a universal individual decision appeal. Stored plain text contains amendment remnants, so changed membership details are not used as evidence.
cases.selection_reason: Baseline topic 3 high-weight education case from a different jurisdiction.

passages.end: summarizing the task force's activities and recommendations.

cases.applicable_actor: Colorado Electronic Discovery in Criminal Cases Task Force and participating agencies.
cases.regulated_action: Study of electronic-discovery costs, tools and equitable access, including AI transcription.
cases.concrete_requirements: Gather information on discovery services and access; study AI transcription availability; submit findings, recommendations and legislative proposals to budget and technology committees.
cases.differences_and_limits: AI is only one part of a broader electronic-discovery study. Agency information-sharing duties have legal and individual-rights exceptions. A common institutional approach does not establish common substantive AI safeguards.
cases.selection_reason: Baseline topic 3 high-weight Judicial Use case; provides a boundary case for the claim of specifically AI governance.
